title: RippleMem: From Isolated Retrieval to Associative Recollection for Long-Term Agent Memory
abstract: arXiv:2608.13334v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM-based agents increasingly rely on external memory to support long-horizon reasoning and interaction. However, the main bottleneck is not simply storing past experience, but recovering the right set of evidence when relevant information is distributed across many interactions. Existing approaches struggle with this access problem. Full-context methods require noisy long-context search, flat retrieval often returns isolated and incomplete records, and graph-based memory systems can be expensive to construct while compressing rich event context. We introduce RippleMem, a long-term memory system that replaces one-shot retrieval with adaptive associative recollection. Inspired by cue-dependent episodic retrieval and associative completion, RippleMem stores interaction history as cue-rich episodic memory units and organizes them in an event-centric memory graph. translated_title: RippleMem：从孤立检索到关联回忆的长期智能体记忆
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.13334v1 公告类型：新论文  摘要：基于大型语言模型的智能体越来越依赖外部记忆来支持长期推理和交互。然而，主要瓶颈并非简单地存储过去的经验，而是在相关信息分布在不同交互中时，恢复正确的证据集。现有方法难以解决这一访问问题。全上下文方法需要嘈杂的长上下文搜索，扁平检索通常返回孤立且不完整的记录，而基于图的记忆系统在压缩丰富事件上下文时可能构建成本高昂。我们引入了RippleMem，一种长期记忆系统，用自适应关联回忆取代一次性检索。受线索依赖的情境检索和关联完成的启发，RippleMem将交互历史存储为富含线索的情境记忆单元，并将其组织在事件中心的记忆图中。给定查询时，它首先通过混合线索回忆相关的记忆锚点，然后进行关联扩展，以逐步恢复更完整的证据集。
tldr: RippleMem通过线索丰富的情境记忆单元和事件中心记忆图，实现自适应关联回忆，有效解决长期记忆中证据分布不均的访问问题。
en_tdlr: RippleMem enables adaptive associative recollection using cue-rich episodic memory units and an event-centric memory graph, effectively addressing the access problem of distributed evidence in long-term memory.
